purpose: Explain kache shared-edit lead: reproduce Nano cold then shared parser edit with per-request capture and compiler phases.
finding: Under the trace, Nano adds about 0.26 s to the harness-ui miss (25.57 s total, rustc 25.31 s). The reproduced shared edit took 112.97 s with no kache daemon running. In both study samples, Nano shared-edit builds immediately followed a kache empty-cache reference build whose cleanup restarts the private kache daemon on the restored store; harness-ui then took 29.25-30.24 s. The runner now waits, outside timing and for every implementation, until that daemon is idle.
limitations: Single traced diagnostic sample with tracing overhead and without the preceding leaf edit; not a speed comparison.

controlled_harness_ui_recompiles.method: Same target directory and edits; cargo clean -p harness-ui; harness-ui and dependents recompiled through Nano with an empty cache (miss path) or NANOCOMPILE_DISABLE=1 (bypass), on Nano-restored dependencies or an rsync byte copy of them; traced and untraced.
controlled_harness_ui_recompiles.finding: harness-ui takes 25.0-25.9 s in every condition; Nano miss path adds about 0.3 s over bypass; restored versus byte-copied inputs make no difference. The 29.3 s seen in all three study shared edits is not reproduced outside the study.

study_sample_3: A pre-build idle wait for the kache daemon did not change the result (Nano 119.833 s, kache 116.993 s; harness-ui 29.36 s). The edit runner now stops the private kache daemon before direct and Nano builds and runs it only for kache builds.
